title: Build the topic vocabulary and assign families to topics
description:

Build notes/topics.tsv as a curated vocabulary the generator validates against, then assign each family to zero or more topics by matching the vocabulary against title, abstract, scope note text, and Lean module path. Emit index/topics/<term>.md listing the families, and print the unassigned-term report so the vocabulary grows from evidence rather than from guesses.

Follow the conditional-tag discipline: a topic term is quotable only after it discriminates. The conditional regex flagged 9 families and 5 were not assumptions, so report per-term yield and quote the false positives. Topics are a column and a page, never a replacement for shapes.

title: Fix the index schema: node and edge tables, store format, location
description:
Decide before rendering anything. The node set is fixed by the release: 372 families, 722 manuscripts, 23 Lean discipline dirs, 554 Lean module dirs, 405 comparator challenges, 178 unique main_results configs, 235 scope notes, 10 traces, 30 verification dirs. The edge set: family->manuscript (722), family->discipline (372), manuscript->Lean file (162 formalized), family->challenge (405), config->declaration (185), manuscript->cited work (12,928 bib entries), plus the derived topic and name edges.

Open forks to settle, in order:
1. Store. Generated markdown plus TSV edge lists in git (reviewable, greppable, byte-identical regeneration, stdlib only) is the recommendation. A graph database is not: ~2,700 nodes and ~17,000 edges is a dict lookup, and Neo4j/Kuzu/Memgraph add a server, a binary store that cannot be reviewed in a diff, and a dependency the generator rules exclude. SQLite (stdlib sqlite3) is the middle option and belongs in a later child, built on demand from the TSV, not tracked.
2. Location. Root index/ is discoverable from README.md; notes/index/ keeps it beside the ledger. Pick one.
3. Granularity. Per-family pages (372) is the floor; per-manuscript pages (722) only if the manuscript page carries something the family page cannot.
4. Topic vocabulary. Curated file the generator validates against, versus auto-derived terms, versus the Lean module path hierarchy alone.

Record the decision in notes/index-design.md with the measured sizes that justify it.

title: Add an on-demand SQLite FTS layer over the manuscript corpus
description:
Only if the TSV index proves too blunt for term queries. notes/scripts/build_index_db.py builds a SQLite database with an FTS5 table over the 7,729 .tex files (128 MB) plus the 372 family abstracts, from the tracked TSV edge lists. The database is a generated artifact: gitignored, rebuilt by script, never committed.

This is the layer that answers "manifold" inside manuscript bodies rather than in titles, and it is the honest answer to the graph-database request: stdlib sqlite3, no server, no binary in git, and the same TSV as the source of truth. Measure query time for a 128 MB FTS build and report it before recommending the layer as routine.
